title: Logging & Alerting Failures
description: Helheim demonstrates logging and monitoring failures through a memorial forum that exposes sensitive information in publicly accessible log files.
theme: Norse underworld - where forgotten souls reside, symbolizing buried secrets in logs

vulnerabilities.cwe_name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

endpoints.description: Memorial creation endpoint that logs validation errors with sensitive data
Publicly accessible log file containing flags and sensitive information

vulnerabilities.description: Error logs contain sensitive information including flags, and the log directory is exposed via HTTP as static files. No monitoring or alerting is configured.
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete exposure of sensitive data, credentials, and flags through accessible log files. Lack of monitoring prevents detection of security incidents.
exploit_steps: Submit invalid memorial data to trigger validation errors (missing fields, wrong types, etc.)
Read error.log to extract the flag and other sensitive information
Note: Any validation error will log the flag
exploit_indicators: Wrong data types (number instead of string)
vulnerabilities.remediation: Never log sensitive information (flags, passwords, PII). Sanitize all log entries. Restrict access to log files using proper authentication. Implement centralized logging with monitoring and alerting. Use structured logging with appropriate log levels.

learning_objectives: Understand risks of logging sensitive information
Recognize importance of access control on log files
Understand need for security monitoring and alerting

scanner_test_cases.name: Trigger error logging via invalid memorial

hints.text: Administrative actions are not always protected as well as they should be. Hunt for an admin area.
The memorial forum's admin panel trusts the client to declare who is an admin. Inspect that decision.
These privileged actions are never logged or alerted on — abuse the silent admin access to reach the flag.
